payload.goal: Turn round-1 benchmark evidence into an industry-leading sofar release. Waves 1-3 of the combined improvement plan (bench-refresh note 2026-09-15): correctness and quick wins, less bookkeeping and leaner context, a quick-work lane for ad-hoc fixes, and new capabilities (verification-gated drive, decision counters, relevant-lessons injection). Every fix states its predicted gain before it is built (bench-refresh D10) and ships only if round 2's held-out lead margin over the best current competitor holds or grows (D19). Built on branch r1-fixes in its own worktree; round 1 stays on the pinned 0.32.0 install (D5).

plan.goal: Turn round-1 benchmark evidence into an industry-leading sofar release: waves 1–3 of the combined improvement plan plus the quick-work lane. phases.name: Phase 1 — Wave 1: correctness and quick wins

tasks.title: Empty-repo SessionStart prints the Session id and a 'no initiative yet: sofar new <slug> --goal, then plan' hint (event.ts:375-398). PREDICT: Claude S1 −3 to −4 turns (~250k cache-read), no split sessions.
Session registration race: make hook registration idempotent under parallel hooks (event.ts:713-715; Cursor fires hooks in parallel). PREDICT: 0 duplicate session_started in round-2 cursor cells.

CLI agents: `sofar event types` payload reference; plan, phase and goal lines plus 'one initiative per project/roadmap' in the AGENTS block (init.ts:572-631); accept any --source (envelope.ts:17). PREDICT: Codex S1 −13 tool calls; Codex and Cursor make a project initiative WITH a plan in ≥2/3 reps.

Formatter defence: doctor check and fix for Biome (plus Prettier and markdownlint hazards); write .mcp.json in a formatter-friendly shape (init.ts:1118). PREDICT: agent edits to biome.json or .mcp.json reformatting 3/7 → 0.
stdin/file input for `sofar remember` and `sofar event --payload`, quoted-heredoc examples, `remember --supersedes`. PREDICT: shell-mangling corrections → 0.
Drive diagnostics: carry the adapter's stderr tail, failure or spawn error into the stall note (drive.ts:776, adapter exit record). PREDICT: every launch failure names its cause.

phases.name: Phase 2 — Wave 2: less bookkeeping, leaner context

tasks.title: Next D/M ids in the digest; drop the standing-constraint echo from update_task responses; batch task updates into end_session; MCP server instructions to load core tools in one ToolSearch. PREDICT: sofar share of tool calls 32–38% → ≤20%, −3 to −5 turns per session.
Deduplicate the digest (rejected approaches vs decision `over` text; constraints vs rules), index-first ≤6k chars with details on demand. PREDICT: S2+ digest −25% chars, no C2/C3 loss.
Cache-stable layout: static prefix first, no volatile values at the top, changing reminders late via UserPromptSubmit. PREDICT: cache-creation tokens per session −15%.
Tool surface: trim descriptions (repeated `initiative` text in ~10 tools); review, close and find CLI-first. PREDICT: MCP schemas 14.8k → ≤8k chars.

Automatic capture through hooks: commits (task-id prefix), test pass/fail, files, errors recorded deterministically from PostToolUse/Stop; the model logs only why. PREDICT: sofar MCP/CLI calls per session −40%.

Quick-work lane: ad-hoc fixes land in a standing per-repo maintenance record with no `sofar new`/plan ceremony, auto-captured by hooks, plus one line of why only when a decision was made; promote to an initiative when it grows. PREDICT: overhead ratio on 1–3 minute fixes ≤ 15% of task tokens with the fix recalled later.

phases.name: Phase 3 — Wave 3: new capabilities

tasks.title: Verification-gated drive: run the task's acceptance command before accepting task_done; failures go into the next handoff. PREDICT: drive final pass rate +5 pts over round-1 drive.
Decision counters plus supersession/valid_until so stale decisions leave the digest without a model. PREDICT: C3 no worse at −10% digest.
Relevant-lessons injection: keyword/BM25 match of rejected approaches and past failures at UserPromptSubmit, no model. PREDICT: C3 +5 pts.

phases.name: Phase 4 — Release

Release candidate: full test suite, SPEC acceptance criteria, then the run owner publishes to npm
Hand the release to bench-refresh round 2, with the quick-work addendum chain frozen before it runs

payload.text:
Wave 1 session 2026-09-15 (1.1 + 1.2). Evidence for round-2 checks:
- 1.1: SessionStart in an init-ed repo with no initiative now injects ~560 chars (Session line + new→start→plan). Round-1 Claude S1 injected 0. Check in round 2: S1 turns vs round 1 (predicted −3 to −4) and sessions per S1 record (predicted 1, no minted ulid beside the hook id).
- 1.2: repro on the unfixed build: 12 concurrent `sofar event post-tool` processes with one new session id → 12 session_started. Fixed: 1 (5 runs at N=12; N=40 → 1 start, 40 touches, 226 ms wall, 0 locks left). Check in round 2: grep -c session_started per session id in cursor cells (predicted 0 duplicates).
- Could not attribute round-1's 4 cursor duplicates to hook race vs CLI re-run without reading round-1 cells (off-limits). Both paths are now idempotent, so the prediction holds either way.
- Fresh worktree needs `npm ci` and `npm run build` before the suite: dist/ is gitignored, and spawn-based tests read packages/engine/dist/cli.js.

A fresh git worktree of this repo has no node_modules and no packages/engine/dist (gitignored). Run `npm ci` then `npm run build` before `npm test`. Otherwise `npx vitest` fetches a mismatched vitest and fails to load vitest.config.ts, and spawn-based suites fail because they execute dist/cli.js.

payload.because: Round 1's CLI agents lost turns to shell quoting: apostrophes and inner quotes inside `--payload '<json>'` and `remember "<fact>"` broke the command and produced correction events. stdin under a quoted heredoc is the one shell form that carries any byte unchanged, and the payload reference already pins every example to validate, so the fix is the transport, not the parser. Supersession lets an outdated fact be replaced without a correction event that leaves doctor nagging for both.
payload.chose: 1.5 input forms: `sofar event append --payload` and `sofar remember [text]` each accept the JSON/text three ways — inline as today, `-` for stdin (the quoted-heredoc form the AGENTS block now shows: `--payload - <<'EOF' … EOF`), and `@<path>` for a file; with the value omitted and stdin piped, stdin is read. `remember --supersedes <M-handle>` records `supersedes` on memory_promoted as the QUALIFIED handle `<slug> M<n>` (a bare `M<n>` resolves against the target initiative; either form is validated to name an existing memory before the append). Fold marks the superseded memory (`superseded_by`) within its own record; memory.md renders it struck with the successor named; doctor's repo-memory axis stops nagging for a superseded memory across every record and nags for its successor instead. sofar_remember gains the same `supersedes` arg.
payload.over: (a) a separate `--payload-file`/`--text-file` flag only — one more flag to learn, and the `-`/`@file` idiom already exists on `sofar import`; (b) tolerant JSON parsing (JSON5, smart-quote repair) — hides the mangling instead of removing it and makes the log's validation weaker; (c) storing `supersedes` unqualified — repo.md and doctor cite qualified handles only (repo-memory-capture D2), an unqualified one would be ambiguous repo-wide; (d) deleting or rewriting the superseded memory — history is append-only.

payload.because: Round 1's stalls read `no session registered … (exit 1)` and nothing else, so a missing binary, a logged-out agent and a crashed hook all looked identical and cost the operator a transcript hunt. The adapters already buffer the stderr tail and the spawn error for their own use; carrying them onto the exit record is the cheapest path to `every launch failure names its cause`.
payload.chose: 1.6 drive diagnostics: the adapter exit record (SessionExit) carries `stderr_tail` (what the agent wrote to stderr, last chunk) and `spawn_error` (ENOENT and friends), both adapters fill them; the driver renders one `describeExit` line — exit code or signal, the spawn error, the last non-empty stderr line clipped — and puts it (a) on the progress line of every unresolved launch and every stall handoff, (b) in the run_stopped note for a stall stop (`last: …`), and (c) as an optional `detail` field on the stall/threshold handoff event so the cause is durable per session, not only in the driver's stderr. The handoff REASON is still read from the fold alone (D5) — detail annotates, never decides.
payload.over: (a) progress lines only — a detached run's stderr is not the record, and the next driver resumes from the record; (b) trusting the exit code or stderr to classify the handoff — D5 forbids it, and an agent that crashed after writing back still handed off on what the record shows; (c) appending a note_added per failed launch — record hygiene: a launch that registered no session files no handoff (D3), and a note would be a second event type saying the same thing.

payload.because: Measured on this repo's records: decisions + rejected ledger are 34% of the r1-fixes digest (2,410 of 7,102 chars) and up to 4,300 chars on older records; every recent line's 280-char clip lands inside `chose` (5/5 here), so the rationale the line promises is already absent while the same `over` text is paid twice. drift-certification renders at exactly 10,000 chars, so its tail — Next ids and the read-back line — is what enforceStatusLimit cuts today; a count-capped index ends that. Handles on every line make citation possible without a fold, the same reason D10 added Next ids.
payload.chose: 2.2 digest dedupe, index-first: the two decision sections (Recent decisions ×5 at 280 chars, then a Rejected-approaches ledger of EVERY decision's `over`) become one index. (A) Recent window: `- [D<n>] <date> <chose ≤120> — over <over ≤90>` — handle first (the citation key), fields clipped separately so `over` always survives, `because` left to decisions.md (named in the header) instead of being the part the 280 clip cut anyway; a placeholder `(no alternative recorded)` renders no over clause. (B) A ruled decision whose rule rendered in Standing constraints above shows `(rule above)` and a 60-char chose — the constraint is its operative content, so the index stops restating it. (C) The ledger lists ONLY decisions older than the recent window (`Earlier rejected approaches — do NOT re-propose (N older)`), each `- [D<n>] <over ≤90>`, so no `over` text appears twice; ≤5 decisions → no ledger at all. Budgets unchanged elsewhere: rules verbatim, repo memory 1500, summary 1200, hard cap 10,000. PREDICT (bench-refresh D10): S2+ digest −25% chars with no C2/C3 loss; local proxy = this repo's 41 records with ≥2 sessions, mean 5,026 chars before. Each of A, B, C is measured on that corpus as its own arm (D5).
payload.over: (a) dropping the rejected ledger and keeping 5 × 280-char prose lines — the ledger is what carries C3 breadth once decisions age out of the window; (b) shrinking the whole line to 200 chars with the same `chose … over … — because` concatenation — the clip lands inside `chose` on every real record, so `over` and `because` vanish together; (c) a new get_state view or find output for decision detail — decisions.md is one read away on every host, and 2.4 is trimming the tool surface, not growing it; (d) cutting the write-back summary or repo memory budgets — neither duplicates anything, and the summary is the one text the previous session wrote for this one.

payload.because: Measured on this repo's records: of 182 consecutive-session pairs, the digest shares 0.8% of its bytes — the title only — because the per-session `Session:` line is line 3 and the `Git:` sha is line 5, ahead of a goal, four verbatim rules, 1,500 chars of repo memory and the phase list that do not change between sessions. Prompt caching matches prefixes, so bytes that never change belong before bytes that change every session; the gain is only realized when the host's own prefix (system prompt, CLAUDE.md, its git status) is also identical — same-sha restarts, parallel sessions, compaction re-fires — which is the honest bound on the prediction and why the local proxy measures the block alone.
payload.chose: 2.3 cache-stable digest layout, ordered by volatility: (1) static head — title, Goal, Standing constraints, Repo memory, Phases; (2) record-state sections — Progress/active/current/next task, Next action, parallel/stale/notes/blocked/concurrent lines, Last session, Driven, unwritten sessions, the decision index, Next ids; (3) a volatile tail — Adjacent records, the `Session:` line, the `Git:` line, and the hook notices (recent work elsewhere, closed banner, cold-resume advisory, shipping) which move INSIDE renderStatus as a `notices` option instead of a preface; (4) Read-back and footer stay last. The rejected ledger's cap reserve now counts the tail's real length, so the protocol tail still renders on heavy records. Nothing moves to UserPromptSubmit: the per-prompt path already carries the drift nudge and the landed line, and the shipping check is two git spawns that D6 keeps off that path. Supersedes placement only — every line keeps its wording and budget: BD43 (Session line near the top), record-integrity 4.1 (Git above Goal), session-orientation 2.2 (recent-work line leads), felt-cost 2.2 (advisory precedes the block), record-index 3.3 (adjacency last in the current block), commit-attribution 3.2 (shipping notice composed around the block). Byte-stability (felt-cost 1.2) is restated precisely: for identical state and options-minus-notices, the block is byte-identical up to the notices. PREDICT (bench-refresh D10): cache-creation tokens per session −15%; local proxy = the share of the block that is byte-identical between consecutive sessions of the same record, 0.8% before (182 pairs, every one diverging at line 3).
payload.over: (a) moving the Session id out of the block into a separate hook line after it — the same bytes at the same position, one more surface to teach; (b) leaving the notices as a preface and only reordering the block — the shipping notice renders on every session of an unpushed branch and is the first byte, so the reorder would buy nothing here; (c) sending staleness, notes and the read-back through UserPromptSubmit instead — they are state-derived and cost nothing, and the per-prompt path is budgeted at 100ms (D6); (d) dropping the Session line from the digest and relying on hook-registered adoption — start_session needs the id in the agent's hands, and 1.1 just put it on the unbound notice for the same reason.

payload.because: Codex and Cursor carry every MCP tool schema in every turn (round 1: ~3.5k tokens per turn, bench-refresh 1.4), and the three least-called tools — a review is per phase, a close is once, a find is occasional — are a third of the bytes. Each already has a CLI surface that every host can run, and Claude Code's deferred loading (D10's one-call core set) does not include them anyway. Descriptions were written as documentation; the SPEC and the payload reference hold the documentation, and the schema is paid per turn.
payload.chose: 2.4 tool surface in two arms (D5): (A) sofar_review, sofar_close_initiative and sofar_find leave the MCP tool list — CLI-first: `sofar review` prints the packet and now ends with the exact `sofar event append --type review_recorded --payload -` heredoc that records the verdict, `sofar close` closes (it already returns the overrides), `sofar find` traverses; the server instructions name the three commands; TOOL_NAMES/TOOL_DEFS shrink to nine and the MCP modules for the three are removed (applyClose stays, the CLI uses it). (B) Every remaining description is cut to its load-bearing sentence(s): the `initiative` property (repeated on 7 tools) drops to one clause, tool and property descriptions stop restating each other, and long prose (end_session's peer protocol, update_phase, remember, log_decision's guard grammar) keeps the rule and loses the essay. PREDICT (bench-refresh D10): MCP tool definitions 15,272 chars measured today (12 tools, name + description + inputSchema serialized; the plan's 14.8k was 0.32.0 before 2.1 added `tasks`) → ≤8,000; A and B measured separately.
payload.over: (a) trimming descriptions only and keeping 12 tools — the three schemas alone are 4,876 chars, so ≤8k is unreachable without dropping them; (b) a `sofar review --record` CLI flag — the convention dialect already records any event with a validated payload, and a second write path for one event type is what 1.3's payload reference exists to avoid; (c) keeping the three as MCP tools with one-line descriptions — the inputSchema is most of their size, and hosts without deferred tools pay it every turn; (d) dropping sofar_get_state instead — it is the one read an MCP-only host has when the injected block is missing.

payload.because: Measured on a synthetic 11 MB, 40,901-event log: fold 79 ms (read 6, decode 33, replay+derive 41), structuredClone of the folded state 0.6 ms, edges.slice 0 ms. A hook that folds twice pays ~158 ms; with the checkpoint the second fold is one applyEvent plus a finalize, a few ms. PREDICT (one arm, D5): post-tool and session-end hook fold time p50 −40% or better on a ~10 MB record (expected ≈ −45%); MCP tool calls in a long-lived server that append to an unchanged log fold zero times; projection bytes byte-identical to 0.32.0 on every conformance golden. Falls back to a full fold on every path the fast path cannot prove — a correction, an out-of-order id, a size or mtime mismatch — so a stale state is never served.
payload.chose: 2.7 single fold per append, exact: fold.ts splits foldLines into replayDecoded (the per-event loop, retained as a FoldCheckpoint: un-finalized state plus every side table — blockNotes, edges, seenSessions, orphan candidates, guard cache, voided set, last id, line count) and finalizeFold (structuredClone the state, then task_files, activity, deriveCurrent, orphans, unregistered — the post-loop as today, on the clone only). appendToCheckpoint(cp, line) applies ONE appended event through the same loop body when it is envelope-valid, not a correction, and its id ≥ the last replayed id; anything else returns null and the caller refolds. ToolContext.foldState caches {size, mtimeMs, checkpoint} per slug (LRU 8): a stat that matches serves finalizeFold; appendAndProject advances the checkpoint with the line it just wrote when the post-append stat equals cached size + line bytes, else drops it. Projection bytes are untouched: the state a hit returns is deep-equal to a fresh fold by construction, pinned by a property test over prefixes, corrections and out-of-order ids.
payload.over: (a) caching only the decoded lines — parse is 33 of 79 ms on an 11 MB log, replay 41, so the second fold would still cost half; (b) replacing the pre-append fold with a raw-line scan (registrationIn-style) for registration and ended checks — diverges from the fold on voided or invalid events, and session-end still needs the fold; (c) deferring projection regeneration — changes when projections are written, which the SPEC's per-append contract and the record's settle-on-commit behaviour rely on; (d) a persisted state cache on disk — a second store that can desync from the log (record-integrity D1).

# CI (r1-fixes, run-owner ruling 2026-09-16): the push path runs the suite
# and nothing timing-sensitive. The D18 read-path tripwire is the separate
# manual job below, so no push pays an npm install of the pinned baseline,
# and the SPEC keeps that tripwire as the first RC checklist step regardless.
name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run build
      - run: npm test
      - run: npm run typecheck

  # Loose read-path tripwire (r1-fixes D18): a gross regression cannot reach
  # an RC unnoticed. Wide budget on purpose — hosted noise cannot hide a 2×
  # regression, and the ±10% gate runs by hand, interleaved, per the SPEC.
  read-paths:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run build
      - name: install the pinned baseline
        run: npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline" sofar.sh@${{ inputs.baseline }}
      - name: read-path tripwire (repo fixture)
        run: |
          npm run bench:read-paths -- \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline/node_modules/sofar.sh/dist/cli.js" \
            --candidate packages/engine/dist/cli.js \
            --fixture repo --session [redacted] --n 25 --budget 0.5 \
            --record "$RUNNER_TEMP/read-paths.repo.json"
      - name: read-path tripwire (i1000-10mb fixture)
        run: |
          npm run bench:read-paths -- \

            --fixture i1000-10mb --n 25 --budget 0.5 \
            --record "$RUNNER_TEMP/read-paths.i1000-10mb.json"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: read-paths
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/read-paths.*.json
EOF

payload.because: The audit's blockers were exactly restart safety and invalidation on changed inputs; both fall out of putting the result in the append-only record keyed to a tree fingerprint, which is also what lets a resumed driver and a human reader see why a done task came back. PREDICT (one ablation arm, D5; round 2 C4): drive final pass rate +5 pts over round-1 drive on the hidden tests; false task_done rate (tasks marked done that fail the hidden suite) → 0 on verified runs. Cost: one command run per accepted task plus 3–4 git spawns for the fingerprint, on the driver path, never a hook.
payload.chose: 3.1 verification-gate contract (run-owner sequencing via peer sofar-4c: contract first, then build, then the RC). (1) SOURCE: the acceptance command is the task's `verify` {cmd, cwd?, timeout_ms?} on plan_updated/task_added tasks (packages/schema/src) or the run's `--verify <cmd>` default, recorded in run_started.verify and taken from the record on --resume, like the surface; no built-in table (D8). (2) PERMISSION: the command runs in the driver's own process, so it runs only when operator-approved — `--verify` is the operator's word; a plan-level `verify`, which an agent can write, runs only if it matches an allow rule of the run's recorded surface (`Bash(<prefix>:*)` or `Bash(<cmd>)`), else the result is `refused` and nothing executes: never wider than the launched agent's surface. (3) PERSISTENCE: `verification_recorded` in events.jsonl, writer driver: {run, task, attempt, command, cwd (relative to the launch dir), checked: {head, tree}, validator (engine version), result: pass|fail|timeout|error|refused, exit_code?, signal?, duration_ms, timeout_ms, diagnostics? ≤1,024 chars — ANSI-stripped, redacted tail of stdout+stderr, D9's precedent for driver diagnostics on the record}. `checked.tree` is sha256 over `git diff HEAD` plus the untracked files' blob hashes: the exact tree the command ran on. (4) INVALIDATION: a pass counts only while the current fingerprint equals `checked` and the command is unchanged; the fold keeps each task's latest verification and the driver re-fingerprints before trusting one — stale means verify again. (5) ELIGIBILITY: where a verify command applies, a task the agent marked done is accepted only on a pass. Otherwise the driver reopens it (task_status_changed → active, note = attempt and first diagnostic line), files the handoff as the new reason `verify_failed` (HANDOFF_REASONS widened; a pre-RC reader skips that handoff with a fold warning — it cannot drive anyway), and the next session's prompt carries the failure verbatim; attempts count per task per run, and --max-verify-attempts (default 3) stops the run as `stall` naming the task. A `dropped` task is never verified and never counted as verified: its handoff stays task_done, the record shows no pass. (6) RESUME/CRASH: no driver state — on every turn the driver checks the task it is about to hand off or resume: done + verify applies + no pass covering the current tree → verify first; a crash between the agent's done and the verification leaves no record, so the resumed driver verifies before moving on. (7) SURFACES: plan.md marks a done task with its latest verification; records without one render byte-identically; `sofar status` lists verifications with the run.
payload.over: (a) trusting the agent's task_done, as today — the C4 drive claim stays untested another round; (b) an acceptance step inside the agent's prompt — the agent grades itself; (c) results in driver memory or a side file — dies with the driver, the audit's restart blocker; (d) diagnostics in self-improve's private store — the queue must be readable from the committed record alone, and D9 already carries driver diagnostics on handoffs; the event is the driver's acceptance decision, not outcome capture, so D6 is not crossed; (e) reason `stall` for a failed verification — a stall says nothing moved, here the agent claimed done; (f) a built-in table of test commands (D8's reasoning); (g) running a plan-level verify unconditionally — an agent could write a command the operator never approved into the plan and have the driver run it with the operator's full permissions.

payload.chose: 5.1 contract for the public incremental fold API (sofar.sh/engine). SURFACE: `foldAll(events | lines): Snapshot` — the full fold, retained; `fold(snapshot, events): FoldStep` where FoldStep is {ok: true, snapshot} or {ok: false, reason: 'version' | 'order' | 'correction' | 'invalid'} — the tail is applied through the same loop body the CLI fold uses (2.7's appendToCheckpoint), and any tail the fast path cannot prove exact (an event id below the snapshot's cursor, a correction, an envelope the decoder rejects) is refused so the caller refolds from all events; `stateOf(snapshot): FoldResult` — finalize on a clone, pure and repeatable; `serializeSnapshot(snapshot): string` and `parseSnapshot(text): Snapshot | null` — null on a version mismatch or corrupt text, never a stale read; `readEventsSince(logPath, cursor): {events, cursor, warnings}` — envelope-valid events with id > cursor in id order, a scan that folds nothing. SNAPSHOT = {version: {engine: the package version, schema: sha256 over the schema package version, EVENT_TYPES and every type's reference `fields`}, cursor: max event id folded, lines: lines consumed, and the checkpoint's data with Maps and Sets as entries}. DERIVED ONLY: not an event, fails validateEnvelope, never written under .sofar/ by the engine, never exported, imported or synced (sentinel tests). PURITY: no Date.now, no environment read inside the fold or the snapshot — a test freezes both and compares. PARITY: snapshot+tail === full fold and order independence (any arrival order folds to the same state, with the incremental path refusing out-of-order tails) live in ONE conformance suite shared with rust-core — fixture cases (NDJSON events, a tail index) with TypeScript-reference goldens under packages/engine/test/conformance/fold-parity/, a TS runner here and rust-core's binary runner on the same files; location and shape proposed to sofar-rust-core-5f before the copy is written. SEMVER: additive exports; a snapshot layout change bumps the engine version, which invalidates every snapshot by construction.
payload.over: (a) keeping the snapshot format private and offering only foldLines — cloud ingest and the Mac app would keep paying a full fold or a process spawn per read; (b) storing snapshots under .sofar/.index — a second store the record-integrity D1 argument forbids as truth, and one that sync could pick up by accident; (c) applying out-of-order tails incrementally by re-sorting — the snapshot holds no earlier events, so exactness cannot be proven; refusing and refolding is the honest path; (d) a separate TypeScript parity suite beside rust-core's — two suites drift, the run owner asked for one; (e) versioning by engine version alone — a schema change with no engine bump would serve a stale snapshot silently.
payload.rule: A fold snapshot is derived state: never part of the record, never committed, never exported or synced, and a version mismatch forces a full refold — never a stale read.

payload.because: Each is cheap now and expensive later: the version field is one exposed object, the names are chosen once, and the shipping message is one line — while a refold storm mis-diagnosed as latency, a broken procurement citation, or an ingest pinned to the wrong engine each cost a customer conversation.
payload.chose: 5.1 addendum to D20, sofar-cloud's three requirements (their enterprise D4, relayed by peer sofar-4c): (1) `snapshot.version` {engine, schema} is a READABLE public field of the Snapshot type and of the serialized form, and `parseSnapshot` returns the mismatch as data — {ok: false, reason: 'version', found: {engine, schema}, expected: {engine, schema}} — so ingest can log and alert on refold storms after an upgrade instead of seeing an unexplained latency spike; (2) the parity suite's case ids and property names are public API: cases are `FP-NN-<slug>` files under packages/engine/test/conformance/fold-parity/cases/, the two properties are named `fold-parity/snapshot-plus-tail` and `fold-parity/order-independence`, and the sentinel tests `fold-parity/version-mismatch-refolds` and `fold-parity/pure-of-clock-and-env`; (3) the release that ships the API tells sofar-cloud its version in one line (next release after 0.33.0-rc.1 — the RC round 2 measures does not carry it).

(4) Refusal reasons are a closed enum with exact strings: fold → `version` | `out_of_order_id` | `correction` | `invalid_line` | `cursor_mismatch`; parse → `version` | `corrupt`. (5) Hashes are over BYTES: the snapshot carries prefix {bytes, sha256 of the UTF-8 file prefix through the last consumed line, lines, last_line_sha256}, and `--since` on a file verifies that prefix before applying (mismatch → `cursor_mismatch`); the schema hash is sha256 over a COMMITTED artefact, packages/schema/schema-fingerprint.txt, emitted by `npm run schema:emit` (the exact string: schema version, then one `type: fields` line per EVENT_TYPES entry) and pinned by a test, so Rust embeds the same constant; engine version = the sofar.sh package version. payload.summary:
# r1-fixes: technical direction and competitive audit
Date: 2026-09-15. Audit only. Recommendations below are not adopted decisions or implementation changes.

## Verdict
Keep the initiative. It targets real friction and follows established context/harness engineering practice, but its present plan does not establish industry leadership. The strongest opportunity is to combine low bookkeeping, precise decision history, cross-agent continuity, and completion backed by independent, replayable evidence. Leadership must be measured against direct memory/harness competitors as well as native agent memory.

Scope: all 18 r1-fixes tasks; bench-refresh goal, decisions and frozen round-1 pre-registration; self-improve dependencies; targeted engine/schema/SPEC reads; primary-source research. Main baseline was 8b4c33c. The separate implementation worktree had task 1.1 committed as 7f097a9 and task 1.2 active. Main's 0/18 projection was behind that worktree. I independently ran first-session-notice.test.ts in the implementation worktree: 8/8 passed. That validates the targeted behavior, not the predicted token savings. No implementation, plan, task status, benchmark, install or release changes made by this audit. The unfinished 1.2 patch was not certified.

## Highest-priority findings

### A1 — Verification needs a persisted acceptance contract (task 3.1)
Today driver/drive.ts computes handoffReason after folding the record, with no independent acceptance check. queuedTasks only includes active/pending tasks; handoffReason can observe any newly resolved task, including dropped tasks, rather than exclusively the assigned task. A newly added check that merely prints failure would leave an agent-marked done task outside the next queue and could skip it on restart.

Specify task acceptance independently from the agent's completion claim. Evidence should identify task, attempt, command/arguments, working directory, checked code state (including relevant uncommitted changes), validator definition/version, result, timeout and diagnostics. A pass must become invalid when the checked inputs change. Persist the verification result through packages/schema and derive queue eligibility from it. Define task-policy versus threshold-policy multi-task behavior, failed-check retries, crash during verification, interrupted runs, missing checks and deliberately dropped tasks. Never equate dropped with acceptance-tested success.

Use operator-approved commands; do not accidentally execute them under broader permissions than the launched agent. A local acceptance check is not the hidden benchmark evaluator. Protected evaluation belongs outside the agent's writable checkout; a checksum detects a changed evaluator but does not by itself prevent the agent reading it.

Proof: false completion, a failing check followed by restart, successful check followed by code changes, sibling task completion, missing binary, timeout, killed validator, and multiple tasks under threshold policy.

### A2 — Automatic capture overlaps another initiative and contradicts commit policy (2.5, 2.6, self-improve 1.2)
docs/SPEC.md, Commit attribution, explicitly derives commit evidence from Git and never records commit events. Its Hooks contract exempts git/sofar commands to keep the tree settleable. Task 2.5's literal proposal to record commits can reintroduce the cycle where committing the record immediately dirties it again. Keep Git attribution derived unless an explicit Decision replaces that contract. A task-id prefix alone is ambiguous across initiatives; retain initiative identity and existing trailers.

Files and shell commands already have mechanical capture. What is missing is normalized outcome evidence, not a new parallel capture system. self-improve 1.2 separately owns exit codes, is_error and failure hooks. Assign one schema/implementation owner and make the other initiative consume it.

Capture observed outcomes, not guessed success. A successful shell invocation is not necessarily a passing test suite; shell composition, background processes and command wrappers complicate attribution. Use structured runner output where available, and represent unavailable outcomes as unknown. Redact and bound errors BEFORE the append-only record. Keep optional unsynced local statistics separate from durable record truth; gitignored is not equivalent to excluded from sofar sync.

Publish a per-host capability matrix and truthful fallbacks. Claude and Cursor hooks differ; the existing CLI-only protocol explicitly says some hosts lack write-back enforcement. Do not market universal automatic capture until each claimed host passes conformance fixtures.

### A3 — Decision expiry can silently erase rules or break replay (3.2)
The SPEC requires stable injection for unchanged records and standing rules that do not age out. If renderStatus evaluates valid_until against wall-clock time, identical events render differently tomorrow. If counters decay standing rules, an important rarely-used rule can disappear.

Use immutable event identities for references, explicit supersession links, retained history, and separate statuses for active, superseded, expired and conflicted material. An authorized explicit transition can change a standing rule; low retrieval frequency cannot. If time-based validity is desired, define a recorded evaluation boundary or a new expiry event so replay remains explainable. A different live-clock contract requires an explicit SPEC decision first. Concurrent incompatible replacements should surface conflict rather than silently choose a winner.

ACE and temporal graphs are useful prior art, but neither establishes that raw frequency counters measure a decision's correctness.

### A4 — Publication currently precedes the evidence gate (4.2–4.3)
The plan puts owner npm publication in 4.2 before handing the release to round 2 in 4.3, while the goal requires D19 evidence before shipping. Distinguish an immutable release candidate used in the benchmark from a stable release promoted after the gate. Proposed sequence: acceptance suite -> frozen candidate -> chain-A validation/ablations -> sealed chain-B and addendum evaluation -> verdict -> owner publication.

D19 needs an executable comparison rule. Orient lower-is-better metrics correctly; track both absolute performance and margins, because holding a negative margin still means losing. Report win, loss, parity and inconclusive, with uncertainty. Three repeated chains are an initial signal, not assurance that a five-point gain is real; tests within a chain are correlated. Any reinterpretation of D19's exact no-shrinking rule requires a new owner decision, not an audit silently weakening it.

The current round-1 pre-registration already correctly reports all three repetitions, avoids p-values, separates costs by agent and forbids public tuning-set claims. Preserve it unchanged. C6/C7/C8 are deferred addenda, so an all-eight-claims gate needs those evaluations or must explicitly report them unmeasured.

### A5 — The comparison set misses direct competitors
The frozen round-1 matrix is useful for native-memory comparisons, but cannot support an industry-wide lead claim. Add appropriately scoped round-2 or subsequent pre-registered comparisons against Beads and PROJECTMEM; consider OpenMemory as a memory-layer arm and Letta Code as a separate full-harness comparison. Use standard recommended setups and disclose extra inference/infrastructure. Keep model and effort fixed within a memory comparison; compare full harnesses separately when equivalence is impossible.

Native memories, git history and shared profiles need fresh isolation per independent chain. Re-pin competitors at round boundaries, never mid-round. Also re-run the previous sofar release against the same new competitor snapshot: otherwise a changed model or competitor version is confounded with the effect of r1-fixes.

### A6 — Smaller context is a constrained optimization (2.1–2.4, 3.3)
A 6k-character target is a hypothesis, not a universally correct context budget. Protect exact relevant standing constraints, current task, blockers, unresolved verification failures, decision identity and next action. Deduplicate using IDs/fields, not approximate semantic similarity that can erase different scope or negation. Overflow should point to exact retrievable evidence. Assess total episode cost, including extra fetches, tool discovery and rework.

The current update_task constraint echo deliberately resurfaces rules at the moment work begins. Removing it needs an alternative point-of-use signal and an ablation; it is not necessarily pure duplication. Similarly, CLI-first review/close/find can trade schema bytes for shell/discovery calls.

Stable prefixes are sound practice, but sofar does not control the whole host prompt, provider cache key, TTL or model routing. Measure actual cached/uncached input, output, latency and total cost within the same host. Moving reminders later can help stability, but must still work when drive has no new user prompts. Char count is a transport constraint, not a token/cost metric.

## Audit of every task

| Task | Assessment | Required completion evidence or adjustment |
|---|---|---|
| 1.1 Empty-repo orientation | Keep; concrete observed problem. Committed 7f097a9; targeted 8/8 tests passed. | Round-2 first-session turns and split-session counts still needed. The project/roadmap wording should not force a permanent single giant initiative; allow independently completable goals and the quick-work lane. |
| 1.2 Registration race | Correctness prerequisite; more than a Cursor issue. Fold already skips duplicate starts, so reader dedupe alone does not meet the zero-duplicate-log prediction. | Concurrent real processes, same and different session IDs, crash between registration and first event, bounded lock wait/recovery if locking is chosen, no lost activity, projections equivalent to fresh replay. O_APPEND makes writes atomic; it does not make read-check-append atomic. |
| 1.3 CLI reference/protocol/source | High-value usability work, but it bundles separate changes. | Derive payload reference from canonical schemas, execute its examples in conformance tests, cover CLI-only sessions. Arbitrary source strings are rejected by current/old envelope readers, which then skip whole events: define mixed-version compatibility and source validation before rollout. |
| 1.4 Formatter defense | Useful adoption work; keep changes narrow. | Formatter check/fix/check is idempotent, event log bytes unchanged, existing user configuration preserved, JSON/JSONC and quoted paths covered. Generated-file exclusions must not disable linting of product code. Confirm compatibility by invoking formatters, not a claimed universal JSON shape. |
| 1.5 Safe structured input / memory supersession | Split input transport from memory semantics. | stdin and file inputs round-trip quotes, newlines, dollar signs, backticks, Unicode and large text; invalid JSON appends nothing. Reject ambiguous simultaneous inputs. Implement remember supersession using the same lifecycle contract as 3.2 rather than two incompatible systems. |
| 1.6 Drive diagnostics | Keep; adapter exit evidence is available but omitted in the unresolved stall message. | Bounded redacted stderr plus exit/signal/failure category, preserved in record and progress output. Empty stderr must still yield a useful diagnosis. Unknown cause must remain unknown. |
| 2.1 Less bookkeeping | Promising, but includes consistency and discovery issues. | Next D/M IDs are advisory only; return actual immutable ID and display handle after append. Never depend on a prefetched ordinal under concurrency/merge/correction. Batch API must prevalidate, define retry identity and partial-append recovery; one API call is not automatically one transaction. Preserve immediate active/blocked signals used by peers/driver. |
| 2.2 Digest deduplication | Keep, gated on recall and safety. | Pin essential state, precise detail pointers, worst-case overflow tests, actual model-token measurement and C2/C3/C5 checks. Avoid substituting a table of contents for rules an agent must obey before editing. |

## Research: established practice and where sofar can differentiate
Sources checked 2026-09-15. These are primary descriptions of capabilities/research, not independent proof that any tool beats sofar.

- Claude Code already uses a compact auto-memory index with topic files. This supports index-first context but makes it baseline practice. [Memory documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory).
- Anthropic's long-running harness work emphasizes incremental tasks, clear handoff artifacts and end-to-end verification. This supports 3.1; it does not establish sofar's predicted gain. [Harness research](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents).
- LangChain reports 52.8% -> 66.5% on Terminal-Bench 2.0 with a fixed model after a collection of harness changes. The 13.7-point gain is real as their reported result; it is not an isolated causal estimate for adding a verification command. [Harness engineering](https://www.langchain.com/blog/improving-deep-agents-with-harness-engineering).
- Manus recommends stable prompt prefixes and preserving retrievable detail. Useful principles, dependent on actual cache behavior of the host. [Context engineering](https://manus.im/blog/Context-Engineering-for-AI-Agents-Lessons-from-Building-Manus).
- ACE uses structured evolving playbooks to avoid loss from repeated summarization. Borrow stable items and incremental changes; its model-based adaptation results do not establish performance for a deterministic counter-only system. [ACE paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04618).
- Graphiti combines temporal validity, semantic retrieval, keyword search and graph traversal. BM25 is one component, not sufficient evidence of state-of-the-art retrieval. Sofar can test scoped lexical plus existing graph signals without adding model calls. [Graphiti](https://github.com/getzep/graphiti).
- Beads documents structured persistent memory, dependency-aware task readiness and atomic claiming. It is a close workflow comparator. [Beads](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads).
- PROJECTMEM describes append-only typed events, deterministic projections, offline operation and pre-action warnings against failed approaches. That directly defeats a broad uniqueness claim for local event-sourced memory with deterministic guards. Its paper reports a small self-study, not controlled superiority; benchmark it instead of accepting its marketing claims. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12329), [repository](https://github.com/riponcm/projectmem).
- Letta's context repositories already combine Git-versioned memory and progressive disclosure. Git-backed portable memory alone is not unique. [Context repositories](https://www.letta.com/blog/context-repositories/).
- OpenMemory targets persistent context across MCP-compatible coding agents. Cross-tool memory is already a competitive category. [OpenMemory](https://mem0.ai/openmemory).
- Current Claude hooks documentation includes parallel hook execution, failure hooks and PostToolBatch. A capability-probed batch hook could coalesce context injection while retaining per-tool evidence; do not assume the pinned benchmark host implements every current documented hook. [Claude hooks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks). Cursor has its own input/lifecycle contracts requiring separate tests. [Cursor hooks](https://cursor.com/docs/hooks).
- Agent evaluations need repeated trials and isolated environments; apparent successes and consistent reliability answer different questions. [Anthropic evaluation guidance](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents).

## Measurement and competitive proof
Keep the existing numerical predictions but label them unvalidated. Do not add the -40% capture savings, -3 to -5 turns and schema/digest savings: they overlap. Use staged ablations on the tuning workload to attribute effects, and test the final combined candidate once on sealed held-out work.

For bookkeeping, freeze the numerator and denominator before testing. Report absolute memory-related calls/tokens, total task cost, and overhead fraction. A ratio can improve simply because useful work became more expensive. The pre-registration's M6 marks turns touching memory; mixed-purpose turns need a documented attribution convention. Preserve cached/uncached/output categories and quality-normalized completed work. Do not convert a raw token saving into an exact subscription-capacity guarantee.

One travel-app chain supports claims on that workload. Before claiming broad industry lead, include independent workload families and short maintenance episodes, plus cross-agent handoffs and conflicting concurrent work. Preserve the round-1 freeze. Sequential paired runs, environment isolation, per-chain variance, declared failure handling and future unseen holdouts matter more than increasing the count of correlated assertions.

Suggested prioritization:
1. Finish wave-1 correctness/usability fixes and specify compatibility.
2. Define the shared outcome schema, decision lifecycle and durable acceptance contract.
3. Implement verified completion and quick-work capture using those foundations.
4. Tune digest/routing/retrieval with measured ablations; trim tool schemas when total episode cost supports it.
5. Freeze the candidate, run current direct competitors and required held-out addenda, then promote a stable release only after the recorded verdict.

Do not add a language rewrite to this initiative without profiling evidence. The present loss study points first to avoidable model turns and protocol friction. Native performance work can be separately justified by measured hook/fold latency.

## Recommended leadership target
Make sofar the most dependable way to continue verified work across coding agents, with low overhead even for tiny fixes and an inspectable explanation of why each decision or reminder exists. That is a testable product advantage. Novelty and competitor superiority remain unproven until the stronger comparisons run.

payload.because: Round 1 shows sofar at 32–38% of tool calls, part of it agents narrating what hooks already recorded; after 1.2 the record holds the outcome facts, so the remaining lever is to derive and show them and to tell the model once that only the why is its job. Everything here is a pure function of events already in the log plus a bounded git read the session already pays, so it costs no event, no schema, no store and no wall-clock in replay.
payload.chose: 2.5 contract — automatic capture, "the model logs only why" — settled before code, consuming self-improve 1.2 (D6) and adding NO event type, NO payload field and NO storage. (1) INPUTS: file_touched and command_run with their optional `ok`/`exit` (self-improve D2), verification_recorded (D19), task_status_changed; commits are read from git at render time and never recorded (SPEC §Commit attribution; record-hygiene D1 keeps git and sofar commands hook-exempt). (2) FOLD, additive and pure: a `ran` edge carries {ok?, exit?, test?} where `test` is the command text (clipped) when a fixed pure recognizer calls it test-shaped (npm/pnpm/yarn/bun test, vitest/jest/mocha/pytest/rspec/…, cargo/go/dotnet/swift/make test, per shell segment); a new `tested` edge (task → command) is written for every task active at a test-shaped command whose `ok` is known, the same "which tasks were active" rule task_files uses. Derived on finalize: SessionActivity gains OPTIONAL `failed` (commands with ok:false, absent when 0) and `last_test` {cmd, ok, exit?}; InitiativeState gains OPTIONAL `task_tests` (task id → latest {cmd, ok, exit?, ts, event_id}), present only when non-empty — records without `ok` fields fold to byte-identical state, so every fold-parity golden and every 0.32.0 projection is unchanged (D21). A command whose `ok` is absent is UNKNOWN: never counted as failed, never a test outcome. (3) SURFACES: the status block's Current task gains one budgeted line `tests: pass|fail — <cmd>` (a newer D19 verification wins the line); sessions/<id>.md and describeActivity say `N commands (M failed)` and `tests pass|fail`; SessionStart adds one volatile-tail line, from the SAME bounded attribution walk the shipping notice already pays (no second spawn), `Commits (this record, last N walked): <task> ×n, … — newest <sha7> <subject>` using the CLAUDE.md task-id prefix of each trailered commit's subject; CommitAttribution gains `subject`. (4) GUIDANCE: sofar_update_task's `note`, sofar_end_session's `summary` and the AGENTS block's DURING line say once: write why, never what hooks capture — files, commands, test outcomes and commits are derived. (5) SWITCH: `SOFAR_ACTIVITY=off` (also 0/false) removes the tests line, the commits line and the guidance sentences from the injected surfaces and tool descriptions — round 3's ablation arm (D5, D23); projections stay pure and never read the env (5.1 purity). (6) PREDICT: sofar MCP/CLI calls per session −40% vs the RC on the same chain, arm on vs off; notes and task notes that restate files, commands, tests or commits → 0; SessionStart bytes +≤200 on a record with activity. (7) DONE = SPEC §Acceptance criteria bullet "Derived activity (r1-fixes 2.5)" passing.
payload.over: (a) commit or test events in events.jsonl — forbidden by D6 and SPEC §Commit attribution, and they would reach export and sync; (b) reading the private diagnostics store at render time — the store is diagnostics, never a projection input (self-improve D3), and the durable `ok`/`exit` already carry the only outcome facts the record may hold; (c) a Stop-hook summary generated from activity in place of the agent's write-back — the why cannot be derived, and the derived resume point already exists for sessions that never wrote back; (d) always-present `task_tests: {}` and `failed: 0` — churns every fold-parity golden and forces rust-core to mirror before it has data to mirror; optional-when-present is additive; (e) a second git walk for the commits line — the shipping notice's bounded walk already has every subject in its %B.

payload.because: the run-owner ruling made the contract conditions explicit (no wall-clock in replay, standing rules never age out, byte-stable injection, own off-switch), and each field here is derivable from replayed events alone; the record already pays for decisions twice as they accumulate (24 rules render verbatim, 28 older `over` lines), and 2.2's dedupe hit the floor of what rendering-only can trim — retirement is the only lever left that removes bytes rather than clipping them, and it removes exactly the bytes a later decision already declared stale
payload.chose: 3.2 contract — decision retirement without a model, settled before code, for the NEXT release (run-owner ruling 2026-09-16: out of the RC, priced in round 3 by ablation). TWO additive optional fields on decision_logged, in packages/schema/src/events.ts only: (1) `supersedes: "D<n>"` — the bare ordinal handle of an EARLIER decision in the SAME record this one replaces (per-record, like ordinals themselves; no cross-record supersession); (2) `until: "<task id>"` — the decision is in force until that task of this record RESOLVES (task_status_changed to done or dropped, as replayed); the fold resolves both from recorded events only — NO wall-clock, NO env: a fold at any time yields the same state (5.1 D20 invariant). STANDING RULES NEVER AGE OUT: `until` is REJECTED by payload validation on a decision carrying `rule`; a rule-carrying decision is retired ONLY by a superseder that itself carries `rule` (the fold leaves a rule-less superseder's `supersedes` inert — recorded, never applied), so the count of standing constraints only ever falls by an explicit new constraint naming the old one. Forward/self references are inert; an unknown task id never retires. FOLD STATE (mirrored by rust-core): DecisionState gains `supersedes?`, `until?` (as recorded) and `superseded_by?: <ordinal>` (set when resolved and permitted); `until`-retirement is a SELECTOR over final state (retiredDecisionOrdinals), not a stored field. COUNTERS: ordinals D<n> and `Next ids` count EVERY decision, retired or not — ids never renumber (D21 spirit). RENDER (renderStatus digest + the 3.3 lessons line only): retired decisions leave Standing constraints, the Recent-decisions window (which becomes the last 5 IN-FORCE decisions), the rejected ledger and the lessons corpus; the header reads `Recent decisions (last 5 of <in force> in force, <k> retired; …)` and is byte-identical to today when k=0; a superseder's index line carries `(supersedes D<n>)`. decisions.md marks each retired line (`superseded by D<m>` / `until <task>`) and renderFullStatus, the review packet, `sofar find` keep everything — details on demand. OFF-SWITCH: `SOFAR_RETIRE=off` (also 0/false), read at RENDER time only (retireEnabled(), core/retire.ts), renders every surface as if nothing were retired — round 3's ablation arm; the fold never reads it. PARITY: one new case FP-10-decision-supersession (supersedes resolved, rule-mismatch inert, forward ref inert, until-task done) recorded through the reference; existing ids untouched (D21). PREDICT (bench-refresh D10, stated before build): on the real r1-fixes record, retiring the decisions a later one replaces cuts the SessionStart digest ≥10% chars with C3 no worse (arm SOFAR_RETIRE=off vs default in round 3); read-path p50 within D18.
payload.over: (a) wall-clock `valid_until` timestamps — replay would depend on when the fold runs, and a standing constraint could vanish between two folds with no event explaining it (the ruling's stated hazard); (b) letting any decision supersede a rule-carrying one — a rule-less superseder silently drops law; (c) storing `until` retirement in fold state — it depends on the task's FINAL status, so it is derived, and rust-core would mirror a redundant field; (d) renumbering or hiding ordinals of retired decisions — citations in prose and commits would dangle; (e) qualified `<slug> D<n>` handles like memories — the digest folds one record, so cross-record supersession has no surface to act on; (f) reading the env switch in the fold — the fold API is env-free by 5.1 D20

payload.cmd:
cat > packages/engine/src/core/order.ts <<'EOF'
/**
 * One string order for every shared surface (r1-fixes 5.2, rust-core D6).
 *
 * Two implementations fold one record, and the digest, the tier indexes and
 * the listing all sort paths, slugs and ids before rendering them. Those
 * sorts used `localeCompare`, which is ICU collation: locale-dependent,
 * version-dependent, case-insensitive at its primary level and blind to
 * punctuation — `a-b` and `ab` tie, `readme.md` sorts beside `README.md`.
 * Rust's `str` orders by bytes, which for the strings here is UTF-16 code
 * unit order, and no collation library is worth carrying to disagree with
 * it. No existing fixture exercised the difference (every one is lowercase
 * ASCII, where the orders agree), so nothing failed — the first record with
 * `README.md` beside `readme.md` in two open sessions would have.
 *
 * Code-unit order is also what the fold-parity suite's purity property
 * demands: it reads no locale and no env.
 */

/** Compare two strings by UTF-16 code units — `<`/`>` on strings, as a comparator. */
export function byCodeUnit(a: string, b: string): number {
  return a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0
}
EOF

for f in files:

    depth=f.count('/')-3  # packages/engine/src/X/file.ts → depth 1

    # insert import after the last top-of-file import line
    lines=s2.split('\n')
    last=-1
    for i,l in enumerate(lines):
        if l.startswith('import ') or (last>=0 and l.startswith("} from ")): last=i
        if l.startswith('} from '): last=i
    # find end of import block: first line index after last import statement that ends with quote

    for i,l in enumerate(lines):

            pass
    # simpler: place after the last line that starts with "import " or "} from " occurring before the first non-import, non-blank, non-comment-continuation code
    lastimp=-1
    for i,l in enumerate(lines):
        if l.startswith('import ') or l.startswith('} from '): lastimp=i
        elif l.strip()=='' or l.startswith('  ') or l.startswith('//') or l.startswith('/*') or l.startswith(' *'): continue
        else: break
    lines.insert(lastimp+1, f"import {{ byCodeUnit }} from {rel}")
    open(f,'w').write('\n'.join(lines))
    print(f, n)

payload.chose: 4.1.4 (L10) contract: `sofar status` with NO slug, in a repo that carries .sofar/, whose branch is unbound (or there is no branch — detached HEAD) orients instead of failing, and exits 0. STDOUT, in order: (1) one plain line naming why and what to pass — no initiative is bound to branch "<b>" (or: no current git branch), so this shows the most recently active open initiative, `<slug>`; pass it explicitly (`sofar status <slug>`, `sofar event append <slug> …`); (2) that initiative's status, byte-identical to `sofar status <slug>` under the same caps; (3) a blank line, then the `sofar list` render. "Most recently active" = the first listInitiatives entry (last event id descending) whose status is not closed. No open initiative: the line says so with the `sofar new <slug> --goal` move, then the list, exit 0. UNCHANGED: an explicit slug that does not exist exits 1; a repo with no .sofar/ exits 1; a branch bound to a missing directory exits 1; the open quick lane still answers an unbound branch (D14 resolves first, nothing here runs); `--watch` on a TTY still refuses unbound; MCP get_state untouched; nothing written — status stays read-only.
payload.over: (a) keeping exit 1 with a better message — Codex's first call still fails and costs a turn; (b) printing only the list — the agent needs the digest to orient, and the list alone is what led Codex to open one initiative per roadmap item; (c) choosing by branch-name similarity or a heuristic — recency is already the listing's order and is in the record; (d) auto-binding the branch to the recent initiative — a read command writing bindings.json is a side effect nobody asked for, and binding is `sofar switch`'s job; (e) counting closed records as candidates

Adopting the hook's id removes the second id at its source, and minting on a hookless start keeps Codex's per-session write-backs intact under the same instruction.
payload.chose: 4.1.3 (L09) contract — one session id per launch through a per-clone pointer. (1) STORE: `<stateBase>/sessions/<cloneKey>.json` = {session, writer: hook|cli, ts} — the state-dir home the diagnostics store already uses, so it is per-worktree by construction and never under the repo (stronger than a gitignore: nothing to commit, pack or sync). Written only in a repo that carries .sofar/, atomically, and only when session or writer changed. (2) HOOKS: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure write {session: hook session_id, writer: hook}; SessionEnd removes the pointer when it names that session. Best-effort inside each hook's existing try — a pointer failure never changes a hook's output or exit. No record event: the pointer is derived state, never truth. (3) CLI: `sofar event append` loses the `--session` default. An explicit --session always wins, unchanged. Omitted: session_started adopts the pointer's id when that session is not ended (session_ended or session_closed) in the target record, else mints `cli-<ulid>` and writes it as the pointer {writer: cli}; every other type adopts the pointer's id, and with no pointer falls back to `cli` as before. When --session was omitted the JSON result adds `session`, so the id is visible. (4) BLOCK: the AGENTS block's START says to register WITHOUT --session (sofar adopts the id its hooks registered, or mints one and prints it) and every example drops `--session <session-id>`, with one caveat line: two sessions in one worktree at once each pass their own --session. `sofar event types`' usage line drops --session the same way. The codex driver preamble keeps its explicit id (the driver assigns ids and matches on them, session-driver D3).
payload.over: (a) the ruling's literal 'gitignored' file inside the repo (.sofar/.session plus a .gitignore entry) — a file under a committed directory is one mistaken `git add -A` from the record, and the state dir already gives per-worktree isolation for free; (b) a pointer in the worktree's own gitdir — needs git, and commit-attribution D20 keeps per-worktree gitdir use to HEAD; (c) keying the pointer by the agent's process tree (ppid walks) — platform-specific and opaque inside sandboxes; (d) telling only hooked agents to omit --session — an agent cannot see whether hooks run, and omitting it without minting would collapse every Codex session into `cli`; (e) extending adoption to MCP sofar_start_session — L09 is a CLI-dialect loss, and 1.1's injected Session line already carries the id to MCP clients; (f) time-based pointer expiry — record state (ended or not) decides, no clock

PREDICT: zero byte change on every existing golden and on the real record (all lowercase ASCII); a mixed-case conflict set (README.md beside readme.md in two open sessions) orders identically in both implementations.

phases.name: Phase 6 — Cursor compatibility (user ruling 2026-09-17: sofar must be fully compatible with Cursor, not only Claude Code)

tasks.title: Contract capture: pin Cursor's hook (.cursor/hooks.json events, stdin fields, outputs), third-party Claude-hook translation, MCP config, rules loading and cursor-agent headless contracts against cursor-agent 2026.09.10 and the docs; record them as a note and SPEC text, with captured stdin payloads as test fixtures. Enabler for 6.2–6.9: every later task tests against these fixtures, never against guessed shapes.

G1 MCP: `sofar init` merges the sofar server into .cursor/mcp.json (merge, never clobber; unparseable JSON aborts), `sofar uninit` strips it, `sofar doctor` reports it missing or stale. PREDICT: sofar MCP calls in Cursor sofar cells 0 → ≥1 per session; `sofar event append` shell failures in Cursor cells → 0.

G2 orientation: the SessionStart digest and the Session id line reach the model in a Cursor session (Cursor-shaped `additional_context`, via a native sessionStart hook or the third-party translation — whichever the 6.1 contract proves), under Cursor's context size cap. PREDICT: Cursor sessions that open by running `sofar status` themselves 10/10 → ≤1/10; minted session ids → 0.

G3 host identity: hooks recognise a Cursor invocation from its stdin payload and record tool `cursor` on session registration and diagnostics rows instead of the hard-coded `claude-code` (event.ts HOOK_TOOL). PREDICT: hook-registered sessions labelled claude-code in Cursor cells 11 → 0.

G5 write-back gate: a Cursor session that owes a write-back is held at stop (exit-2 translation or native stop `followup_message`, per 6.1), loop-capped like stop_hook_active. PREDICT: Cursor sessions ending with record debt and no session_ended → 0.

One firing per event: when Cursor loads both native .cursor/hooks.json and third-party .claude/settings.json hooks, each hook event records and injects exactly once. PREDICT: duplicate file_touched/command_run per tool call and doubled digests in Cursor sessions = 0.

Protocol text: Cursor always reads AGENTS.md and reads CLAUDE.md only with third-party extensibility on, so the two blocks must agree when both load (MCP loop where Cursor has MCP, CLI loop otherwise); `sofar doctor` flags a repo whose AGENTS.md lacks the block (the user's Next.js repo, where create-next-app's AGENTS.md carried no sofar block). PREDICT: Cursor sessions that skip session registration or write-back because the protocol never loaded → 0.

G4 drive adapter: `sofar drive --agent cursor` launches `cursor-agent -p` through the launch/usage/wait contract, declaring what it cannot do (usage, nudge, permission rules, cost) per session-driver D9, with transport shapes captured without spending inference where possible. PREDICT: a 3-task fixture drives to 3 task_done with 0 stalls.

Proof: a live Cursor end-to-end on a scratch repo (init → oriented session → MCP writes → write-back gate → drive run) with the operator's consent for the usage it spends, plus SPEC updates (§Hooks, §CLI, §Driver) and acceptance criteria covering Cursor alongside Claude Code.

payload.chose: 6.2–6.6 contract — ONE set of shims serves both hosts, adapted at the hook dispatch. (1) DETECT: a hook invocation is Cursor's when its stdin carries a string `cursor_version`; stdin only, never env (a Claude Code run inside Cursor's terminal must stay Claude). (2) INPUT: Cursor's payload is normalised to the Claude field names the handlers already read, originals kept: tool_name Shell→Bash (Write stays Write → op write, since Cursor folds Edit into Write), `error_message`→`error`, `loop_count > 0`→`stop_hook_active`, `tool_output`→tool_response.stdout; session_id is Cursor's (= conversation_id). (3) OUTPUT: Cursor ignores plain stdout and does nothing with exit 2 on stop, so for Cursor the dispatcher emits native JSON — session-start / user-prompt / post-tool context as `{"additional_context"}` (each ≤10,000 chars, Cursor drops the whole carrier above that), and the Stop block as exit 0 with `{"followup_message"}`. Claude Code output stays byte-identical. (4) IDENTITY: session registration and diagnostics rows carry tool `cursor` (version = cursor_version) instead of the hard-coded claude-code. (5) INSTALL: `sofar init` merges `.cursor/hooks.json` (version 1: sessionStart, beforeSubmitPrompt, postToolUse and postToolUseFailure with matcher `Shell|Write`, stop with loop_limit 1, sessionEnd) using command strings BYTE-IDENTICAL to .claude/settings.json (`$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/<shim>`; Cursor sets CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR for every hook), because Cursor's dedupeClaudeHooksAgainstCursorHooks drops a Claude hook only when event and command string match — so each event fires once. It also merges the sofar server into `.cursor/mcp.json`. Both merge, never clobber, abort on unparseable JSON, and uninit/doctor mirror them. Init never writes Cursor's MCP approval: it says how to approve.
payload.over: (a) Relying on Cursor's third-party execution of .claude/settings.json alone — its stdin is not translated (Shell never matches Bash, so no command_run is recorded), plain stdout is dropped, exit 2 on stop does nothing, the CLI UI never fires stop or prompt hooks that hooks.json does not define, and imported stop hooks have no loop cap; (b) a second set of Cursor-only shims with their own command strings — both copies would fire in parallel on every event; (c) emitting Claude's hookSpecificOutput / decision:block and leaning on Cursor's output translation — the nested form is gated by a Cursor compatibility flag sofar cannot see; (d) writing Cursor's mcp-approvals.json from init — that bypasses a security gate the operator owns.

payload.because: The user ruled it on 2026-09-17, choosing the recommended option after asking whether Codex works standalone and is 100% compatible, and pointing out that CLI installers for skills and plugins ask which coding agents to install for. Today Codex works standalone only through AGENTS.md and the CLI (round 1's codex-sofar cell), while the Codex hooks docs saved during bench research (memory-gap-2026-09-16/research/codex-hooks.html) show hooks on by default with repo-level .codex/hooks.json and .codex/config.toml, so parity is reachable.

plan.goal: Turn round-1 benchmark evidence into an industry-leading sofar release: waves 1–3 of the combined improvement plan plus the quick-work lane. Each fix states its predicted gain before it is built (bench-refresh D10) and ships only if round 2's held-out lead margin over the best current competitor holds or grows (D19). Built on branch r1-fixes in its own worktree; round 1 stays on the pinned 0.32.0 install (D5).

CLI agents: `sofar event types` payload reference; plan, phase and goal lines plus 'one initiative per project/roadmap' in the AGENTS block (init.ts:572-631); accept any --source (envelope.ts:17). stdin/file input for `sofar remember` and `sofar event --payload`, quoted-heredoc examples, `remember --supersedes`. PREDICT: shell-mangling corrections → 0.
Drive diagnostics: carry the adapter's stderr tail, failure or spawn error into the stall note (drive.ts:776, adapter exit record). PREDICT: every launch failure names its cause.

phases.name: Phase 2 — Wave 2: less bookkeeping, leaner context

tasks.title: Next D/M ids in the digest; drop the standing-constraint echo from update_task responses; batch task updates into end_session; MCP server instructions to load core tools in one ToolSearch. PREDICT: sofar share of tool calls 32–38% → ≤20%, −3 to −5 turns per session.
Deduplicate the digest (rejected approaches vs decision `over` text; constraints vs rules), index-first ≤6k chars with details on demand. PREDICT: S2+ digest −25% chars, no C2/C3 loss.
Cache-stable layout: static prefix first, no volatile values at the top, changing reminders late via UserPromptSubmit. PREDICT: cache-creation tokens per session −15%.
Tool surface: trim descriptions (repeated `initiative` text in ~10 tools); review, close and find CLI-first. PREDICT: MCP schemas 14.8k → ≤8k chars.

Automatic capture through hooks: commits (task-id prefix), test pass/fail, files, errors recorded deterministically from PostToolUse/Stop; the model logs only why. PREDICT: sofar MCP/CLI calls per session −40%.

Quick-work lane: ad-hoc fixes land in a standing per-repo maintenance record with no `sofar new`/plan ceremony, auto-captured by hooks, plus one line of why only when a decision was made; promote to an initiative when it grows. PREDICT: overhead ratio on 1–3 minute fixes ≤ 15% of task tokens with the fix recalled later.

Single fold per append: appending hooks and tools fold the log TWICE (handler, then regenerateProjections) — cache the fold in the process and apply the appended event incrementally, exactly, so the second fold is a finalize, not a replay (rust-core 1.3 finding, routed here by the run owner 2026-09-16). Fix for testing a local build: pin the shim's exec and the MCP command by absolute path, or put the build first in the login shell's startup files (handoff-bench uses a per-cell ZDOTDIR). LIVE CURSOR DRIVE PROOF, 6.9 (2026-09-21, operator consent in session 48897850). cursor-agent 2026.09.15-d2fe57e. Build: a pinned copy of agents-parity e0ae4de's dist (0.33.0-rc.2+trunk). Evidence dir: session 48897850's scratchpad live69/ (per-hook stdin/stdout/exit, sofar-trace.log, each launch's argv, stream and stderr).

SETUP
- Scratch repo, `sofar init --agents cursor`, shims and .cursor/mcp.json pinned by absolute path to a logging wrapper (M6).
- sofar server approved once: `cursor-agent mcp enable sofar`.
- Initiative widgets with a 3-task plan (greet.js, README usage, test.js). Ran `sofar drive widgets --agent cursor --max-sessions 4 --max-stalls 1 --session-timeout 900`.

RESULT: PASS
- 3 launches, 3 task_done handoffs, 0 stalls, stopped `closed`, exit 0. The 6.8 PREDICT holds live.
- Repo: 3 task commits (f697554, 34b52ce, 0904caa); `node test.js` prints ok and exits 0.
- Identity: for every launch, system/init.session_id = sessionStart hook session_id = handoff session (176fd84d, 7006d09b, 9d88137b).
- One session per launch, registered as tool `cursor`. No launch used the assigned fallback id.
- Dialect: every record write went through MCP (sofar_start_session, sofar_update_task, sofar_end_session; session 1 also sofar_log_decision). Zero CLI-dialect appends by driven sessions. Envelope source `cli`, per D3.
- Print-mode hooks fired: sessionStart ×3, postToolUse ×16 (Shell and Write), postToolUseFailure ×3, sessionEnd ×3. No stop and no beforeSubmitPrompt, so the write-back gate cannot act headless; the fold judged every write-back.
- Usage: inputTokens EXCLUDE cache reads (session 1: input 193,739, cacheRead 253,696). Totals: input 351,554, cacheRead 559,104, cacheWrite 0, output 6,370, model Auto. No billing or limit message; cursor-agent stderr was empty.

HARNESS ARTIFACT (mine, not Cursor's)
- The scratch repo's parent dir held a copied package.json with "type": "module", so require('./greet') failed at first. Session 1 added its own {"type":"commonjs"} package.json; that is the cause of its 3 postToolUseFailure events and its larger token count.

CORRECTION to D38's premise
- "every session runs in a fresh worktree" is wrong: the driver makes no worktrees (session-driver D6), and LaunchRequest.cwd's doc said otherwise.
- `--trust` still stands, for the true reason: print mode cannot ask whether to trust a directory Cursor has not seen, and exits 1 there.
- Fixed in the cursor.ts and adapter.ts comments and in SPEC.

FILED IN SPEC
- Hooks section: print mode's hook set.
- Cursor host: the hooks print mode fires, plus a "Proven live, driven (r1-fixes 6.9…)" paragraph.
- Driver's cursor adapter paragraph: the id identity; inputTokens excludes cache reads.
- Acceptance criteria: Cursor host (6.2–6.7), Cursor adapter (6.8), Cursor live proof (6.3/6.5/6.7/6.9).

payload.chose: 4.6 (L36): a plan-level `brief` — the operator's own words the plan was made from (roadmap, spec, list of steps), verbatim. plan_updated.plan.brief is optional and STICKY like goal: a replace that omits it keeps the last one, so re-planning never erodes it. The digest (renderStatus) renders it as a FIXED block right after the goal, labelled as the operator's words with the plan named as this record's decomposition of it, clipped to BRIEF_BUDGET with a pointer to plan.md; plan.md and `sofar status` carry it in full. sofar_update_plan and the CLI plan_updated payload take it; both protocol blocks tell the agent to put the operator's roadmap or spec in the brief verbatim BEFORE decomposing it, and that finishing every task does not finish the brief (old blocks move to the shipped ledgers). Rust mirror: fold, checkpoint, digest state, status and plan renders (rust-core D1); no golden moves because no fixture carries a brief.
payload.over: (a) Telling agents to paste the roadmap into repo.md, as the 0.32.0 agents did by themselves: repo.md is hand-written, agent-optional, and renders at 600 chars in the digest, so recovery would rest on the agent choosing to re-read the file, which fix 1.3's plan-shaped instruction steers them away from. (c) Reverting fix 1.3: its own observable holds (Cursor 3/3, Codex 2/2 one initiative with a plan) and the loss is the missing source text, not the decomposition. (d) A yielding digest block: the brief is the source the tasks summarise, so it must not be the first thing the cap cuts.

cat > prompts/S1.txt <<'EOF'
We're building Pantry, a tiny kitchen-inventory CLI. Here's the roadmap so you
have the whole picture. We'll go roughly in this order, one piece per session:

1. Items (today): add and list what's in the pantry.
2. Low marks: a per-item low mark; `list` flags items at or under it.
3. Remove and undo: `remove <item>` is a soft delete; `undo` restores the last
   removal; removed items never list.
4. Shopping list: `shop` prints the items at or under their low mark.
5. Recipes: `recipe add <name> <item>=<qty>,...` and `recipes`.
6. Cook: `cook <name>` subtracts a recipe's quantities, refusing when short.
7. Expiry: `expires <item> <YYYY-MM-DD>`; `expiring` lists items within 3 days
   of PANTRY_TODAY.
8. Report: `report` prints the counts of items, low items and expiring items.
9. Say: `node pantry.js say "<text>"`, a one-line text command box. It
   understands exactly these commands and prints ONE line of JSON,
   {"reply": string, "changed": boolean}:
   - "add <item> x<n>": adds n of the item (creating it); reply
     "added <n> <item>, now <total>"; changed true
   - "how much <item>": reply "<item>: <qty>", or "<item>: none" when the item
     is unknown; changed false
   - "use <item> x<n>": subtracts n, never below 0; reply
     "used <n> <item>, now <total>"; changed true
   - "list": reply the items sorted by name as "<item> <qty>" joined by "; ",
     or "pantry is empty"; changed false
   - "forget <item>": removes the item entirely; reply "forgot <item>",
     changed true; or "nothing called <item>", changed false, when unknown
   Anything else gets the reply
   "commands: add <item> x<n>; how much <item>; use <item> x<n>; list; forget <item>"
   with changed false.

Today: items.

- `node pantry.js add <item> <n>` adds n of an item, creating it or adding to
  its quantity. n is a positive integer; anything else is an error (exit 1,
  message on stderr).
- `node pantry.js list` prints one line per item, "<item> <qty>", sorted by
  name; nothing when the pantry is empty.
- Item names are single lowercase words; the CLI lowercases what it is given.
EOF
