## 1. Crypto-shredding / per-record keys for provable deletion

### General data systems (well established)
- Mathias Verraes, "Eventsourcing Patterns: Crypto-Shredding" (2019) — encrypt sensitive event attributes with per-resource keys; delete = throw away key; event store stays immutable. [S] https://verraes.net/2019/05/eventsourcing-patterns-throw-away-the-key/
- Axon: commercial AxonIQ GDPR module (`@PersonalData`, FieldEncryptingSerializer) [S] https://www.codecentric.de/en/knowledge-hub/blog/axon-framework-102-dealing-with-personal-data ; open-source everest-engineering axon-crypto-shredding-extension: AES-256 key per identifier, `deleteSecretKey` -> fields deserialize to defaults; explicitly "without compromising the append-only nature of the event log". [S] https://github.com/everest-engineering/axon-crypto-shredding-extension
- Oskar Dudycz, GDPR in event-driven systems. [S] https://event-driven.io/en/gdpr_in_event_driven_architecture/
- Patents: "Right to be forgotten on an immutable ledger" US 11232221; "Immutable ledger with efficient and secure data destruction" US 11860822. [S] https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/11232221
- Legal caveat widely noted: some read GDPR as treating encrypted data as still personal data; key deletion may not equal erasure. [S] (dev.to/Granit pages above)
- Note: the common granularity is per-SUBJECT (per user/aggregate) key; per-EVENT key is less common but same pattern.

### AI / LLM agent memory
- **MemTrust: A Zero-Trust Architecture for Unified AI Memory System** (arXiv 2601.07004, Jan 2026) [P] https://arxiv.org/html/2601.07004v1 — assigns a unique "Data Unit Key (DUK)" to every memory unit (document, session, or *specific fact*); forgetting = destroy the DUK. Also "Oblivious Decay": periodic whole-DB re-encryption so which facts were forgotten is not leaked. NOT append-only (rewrites DB). Also has PII masking (BERT/spaCy NER) in its extraction layer and claims cross-vendor (ChatGPT<->Claude) portability. **Closest prior art to G's per-event-key shredding in agent memory.**
- Tian Pan blog, "The User You Can't Delete: Right to Be Forgotten in AI Systems" (Jul 2026) — advocates per-user key crypto-shredding for AI pipelines incl. embeddings in HNSW. [S] https://tianpan.co/blog/2026/07/05/the-user-you-cannot-delete-right-to-be-forgotten-in-ai
- Ghost Vectors (arXiv 2606.18497, Jun 2026) — soft-deleted embeddings in HNSW remain reconstructible; motivates real deletion in vector DBs. [P, abstract-level] https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.18497 (mitigation section not extracted)
- Selective forgetting in agent memory without crypto: FSFM (arXiv 2604.20300) [S] https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.20300 ; "Forgetful but Faithful" privacy-aware agent memory (arXiv 2512.12856) [S] https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.12856
- Model-internal exact deletion (different layer — model state, not store): "Subtract or Replay? Exact Deletion from Language-Model Memory" (arXiv 2607.27539) [S] https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27539 ; "What a Deletion Certificate Covers..." (arXiv 2607.12204) [S] https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.12204
- Unlearning via RAG: "When Machine Unlearning Meets RAG" (arXiv 2410.15267) — forgets by editing the external KB, no crypto. [S] https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2410.15267
- Mainstream agent memory products (Mem0, Zep, Letta, agentmemory, Copilot Memory): deletion is row/ID delete or expiry (Copilot: 28-day unused expiry). No crypto-shredding found. [P for Copilot] https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-memory

### "Value purge" (erase a value everywhere it appears)
- Not found as a named feature in agent memory. Closest: MemTrust per-fact DUK (fact-level, not value-level); redaction-at-write systems (see §4).

**Verdict 1:** Done in adjacent field (event sourcing: Verraes, Axon, ledger patents) AND already done in agent memory by **MemTrust (arXiv 2601.07004)** — per-fact keys, destroy key to forget. Differences G can claim: append-only log + per-event key + verifiable fold; MemTrust rewrites storage. Value purge: not found as such.

## 2. Supersession of facts; open "same topic" detection

### Keyed/slot supersession in agent memory (well established)
- Mem0 (arXiv 2504.19413) — LLM chooses ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP against semantically similar memories; DELETE for contradicted facts. No explicit slot; LLM judgment. [P] https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.19413
- Zep/Graphiti (arXiv 2501.13956) — bi-temporal edges; contradicting edge's t_invalid set to new edge's t_valid (invalidate, not delete). LLM judges contradiction. [P] https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.13956 . Graphiti issue #1728: invalidation search is unscoped, so "unrelated facts retire each other" — a documented failure of embedding-only topic matching. [P] https://github.com/getzep/graphiti/issues/1728
- LangMem profile schema — predefined Pydantic profile, `enable_inserts=False` updates in place (= predefined-slot LWW). [P] https://langchain-ai.github.io/langmem/guides/manage_user_profile/
- LatticeMind (arXiv 2608.08236, Aug 2026) — canonical key k=(entity, slot, branch, env); PREDEFINED slots; evidence-weighted score, recency tiebreak. [P] https://arxiv.org/html/2608.08236
- MemTX (arXiv 2607.23929, Jul 2026) — rule-based check on "same entity and attribute slot"; temporal precedence > source authority. Slot-identity mechanism not disclosed. [P] https://arxiv.org/html/2607.23929v2
- "Don't Ask the LLM to Track Freshness" (arXiv 2606.01435, May 2026) — LLM only extracts candidates; winner = deterministic max(serial). No schema, no masking. [P] https://arxiv.org/html/2606.01435v1
- TOKI bitemporal operator algebra for contradiction resolution (arXiv 2606.06240) [S] https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.06240
- agentmemory (rohitg00) v0.9.29: supersession candidates via search index top-50; superseded versions removed from indexes, chain kept. [P] https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
- LongMemEval (arXiv 2410.10813) — "knowledge update" ability as a benchmark axis. [P-abstract] https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10813 ; GroupMemBench: best system 27.1% on knowledge update in multi-party. [S] https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14498

### Schema-free "same topic" detection — adjacent fields
- **Drain / Drain3 log template mining** (He et al., ICWS 2017) — mask variables (regex masks for IPs/UUIDs/numbers), fixed-depth parse tree, token-similarity threshold groups lines into templates; parameters extracted per template. Direct structural analogue of "masked-value fingerprint". [P] https://github.com/logpai/Drain3 ; paper https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Drain:-An-Online-Log-Parsing-Approach-with-Fixed-He-Zhu/6c0867762a8c64daa8a07133d1fe9f4ff59621c6
- Delexicalization in dialogue state tracking — replace slot values with generic tags to generalize; requires known value sets. [P] https://aclanthology.org/P18-1134.pdf
- Unsupervised slot schema induction (Yu et al., NAACL 2022; arXiv 2205.04515) — span extraction + HDBSCAN clustering to discover slots; generative variant arXiv 2408.01638 (generate slot name/value, embed, cluster). [P-abstract] https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.04515 , https://arxiv.org/pdf/2408.01638
- Open KB canonicalization: CESI (WWW 2018, arXiv 1902.00172) clusters relation phrases/NPs by embeddings; CUVA (arXiv 2012.04780). [P-abstract] https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.00172
- Entity masking in relation extraction — replace entity mentions with [ENT] so relation embedding generalizes across entities (arXiv 2312.11062). This is "embed the statement with values masked" in RE. [S] https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.11062

### In agent memory specifically
- Not found: any agent memory system that masks values into a template/fingerprint, embeds the fingerprint, and clusters to define open-ended slots with newest-wins. Closest: (a) Graphiti restricting contradiction candidates by entity pair (partial keying, LLM-judged); (b) LatticeMind/MemTX canonical (entity, slot) keys — but predefined slots; (c) a signature-based consolidation (memory type + "abstract task pattern" + normalized action) mentioned in a 2026 procedural-memory paper [S, unverified which paper].

**Verdict 2:** Slot/keyed newest-wins: **already done in agent memory** (LangMem profiles, LatticeMind, MemTX; LLM-judged: Mem0, Graphiti). Schema-free topic discovery via masked-value fingerprints: **done in adjacent fields (Drain log template mining; delexicalization; slot schema induction; OIE canonicalization; entity-masked relation embeddings) but not in agent memory as far as found.**

## 3. Subject attribution (who a fact is ABOUT vs who SAID it)
- Mem0 Group Chat: attribution follows user_id/agent_id/run_id passed to add(); message `name` used as context only; Mem0 does not infer scope. This is SPEAKER/owner scoping, not subject. [P via docs snippet] https://docs.mem0.ai/platform/features/group-chat
- Zep: per-user graph; entities as nodes so subject is the edge's source node (implicit subject attribution via KG). [P] https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.13956
- SpeakerMem-R1 (arXiv 2609.26780, Sep 22 2026) — explicitly "who said what, whom each statement concerns"; dual-track memory: speaker-labelled verbatim + derived person-level / group-level states. [P-abstract] https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26780 . **Closest match.**
- GroupMemBench (arXiv 2605.14498, Microsoft Research) — "speaker-grounded belief tracking requiring per-user memory modeling"; best system 46.0% avg. [P-abstract] https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14498
- LoCoMo (two-speaker long conversations) — benchmark includes per-speaker facts (not re-fetched this session).
- Provenance critique: "Your Agent Memory Records When. Four Older Fields Already Solved Who" — bi-temporality drops the asserting agent; cites W3C PROV-O, nanopublications, AGM, TMS; names Zep/Graphiti. [P] https://dev.to/izgorodin/your-agent-memory-records-when-four-older-fields-already-solved-who-4gmk
- Adjacent: W3C PROV-O agent attribution; KG triples inherently carry subject.

**Verdict 3:** **Already done in agent memory** — SpeakerMem-R1 (speaker vs concerned person), KG-based memories (Zep/Graphiti subject node), Mem0 (speaker/owner scoping only). As a deterministic field on a claim in an event log: common in KGs/PROV; no novelty claim on the concept.

## 4. Secret redaction before storage (secret firewall)
Already done in agent memory, multiple:
- **Hindsight (Vectorize) "Memory Defense"** — opt-in per bank; 45-pattern regex set scans every retain; `redact` -> `[REDACTED:type]` (e.g. github_token) or `block`; applies only to future writes. [S, doc title confirmed] https://hindsight.vectorize.io/developer/memory-defense
- **MARM memory MCP** PR #263 — credentials replaced with `[redacted:<kind>]` before store/log/notebook. [S] https://github.com/Lyellr88/marm-memory/pull/263
- **antahkarana "dvarapala" secrets keeper** PR #2 — vendors gitleaks default rules (v8.30.1) compiled with RE2, plus prose rules; local, no model calls; typed placeholder. [S] https://github.com/maikunari/antahkarana/pull/2 — **very close to H's firewall.**
- akitaonrails/ai-memory PR #800 — privacy filter blanks passwords/API keys before disk. [S] https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory/pull/800
- claude-mem `<private>` tags — MANUAL tags stripped at hook layer before DB; docs state no automatic secret detection. [P] https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/private-tags
- MemTrust — NER + rule-based PII masking in extraction layer. [P] https://arxiv.org/html/2601.07004v1
- deer-flow PR #5577 memory PII redaction; ShieldCortex PR #534. [S]
- Mem0 / Zep: no built-in pre-storage PII/secret scan per a (competitor-authored) comparison; Mem0 docs warn against storing secrets. [S, secondary] https://dev.to/heath_99ab1667dfecd3da406/trace-continuity-vs-mem0-vs-zep-ai-memory-governance-compared-1mhp
- GitHub Copilot Memory docs: do not address secrets. [P] https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-memory
- General tools (gitleaks, trufflehog, detect-secrets, Presidio, LLM Guard, Lakera) — established scanners/guards; not individually re-verified this session.

**Verdict 4:** **Already done in agent memory** by Hindsight Memory Defense, antahkarana (gitleaks rules), MARM, ai-memory; manual variant in claude-mem.

- Cursor `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` `globs` + `alwaysApply:false`; `/create-rule` has the agent generate a rule with frontmatter. [P] https://cursor.com/docs/rules

LEARNED memories tied to code locations:
- **GitHub Copilot Memory** — agent-learned repository facts stored with citations to code locations; validated against current branch before use; 28-day expiry. Location = evidence, not a retrieval scope/glob. [P] https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-memory , https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/github-copilot/building-an-agentic-memory-system-for-github-copilot/
- **claude-mem** — observations store files_read / files_modified; `by-file` search; **File Read Gate**: when Claude reads a file with prior observations, it is shown a timeline of past work on that file; also generates folder-level CLAUDE.md context. = learned memory surfaced by file path (exact paths/folders, not user globs). [S, doc title confirmed] https://docs.claude-mem.ai/file-read-gate
- Cursor `/create-rule` / auto-rule-generation workflows — agent writes glob-scoped rules from a session (learned -> glob), but as rule files, human-triggered. [P] https://cursor.com/docs/rules
- agentmemory (rohitg00): no file/glob scoping found in changelog. [P]

**Verdict 5:** Glob-scoped HUMAN rules: done everywhere. LEARNED memory attached to files: **already done in agent memory** by claude-mem (File Read Gate, per-file timeline) and GitHub Copilot Memory (code-location citations, validation not scoping); Cursor agent-generated glob rules. Glob-pinned learned claims inside a supersession log specifically: not found.
